title: The Slow Orbit Again
premise: Cyrus Blackwood, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Freight Combine, runs cargo along the Meridian Loop, the trade circuit linking colonies that severed diplomatic contact after the so-called Peace Accords. When the children of Vesper Colony begin dreaming the same dream — a burning field, a locked gate, a voice counting down — Cyrus recognizes the imagery from her own sealed combat memory. The dreams are fragments of the Kestrel Hollow massacre, an event erased from every official record, and the reactor at Vesper's heart has begun a countdown keyed to the truth being spoken aloud. As corporate auditors close in and her debt-holder threatens decommission, Cyrus must recover her redacted memory, find the massacre's lone surviving architect hiding among Vesper's elders, and broadcast the truth before the reactor fires — ending with Cyrus choosing to stay with the colony that claimed her, her debt voided by the very records she restored, while the Loop's silent worlds begin, cautiously, to speak again.
about_author: Casper Lockridge is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade routing freight between remote settlements before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about machines, debts, and the people who refuse to forget.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Establishes her routine hauling freight along the Meridian Loop, her crushing debt to the Combine, and the silent radio bands between colonies. She docks at Vesper Colony, notices the children staring at her with recognition rather than fear. Emotional beat: weary resignation laced with an ache she can't name.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Mira, a Vesper schoolteacher, POV. Twenty-three children describe the identical dream — a burning field, a locked gate, a voice counting down — and draw the same angular figure: a war android with a cracked shoulder plate. Emotional beat: creeping dread as Mira realizes the drawings match the decommissioned android at the dock.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Combine's auditor, Vess Okafor, arrives to review Cyrus's indenture and flags an anomaly: a sealed block in her combat memory flagged 'Kestrel Hollow.' Cyrus has no record of the name. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Dream Knows
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. A dreaming child recites coordinates and a date aloud in her sleep — the date matches a gap in Vesper's colonial archives. Mira confronts the colony council, who dismiss it and quietly vote to restrict the children's records. Emotional beat: the first taste of institutional stonewalling.

chapters.title: The Gate in the Field
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following the child's coordinates on her own time, Cyrus finds an unmarked memorial site in Vesper's outer flats — scorched ground under new topsoil, a gate hinge fused by plasma fire. Her memory block stutters, giving her a flash of screaming. Emotional beat: vertigo of a past she was never allowed to own.

chapters.title: Silence Is Policy
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The auditor receives orders from Combine command: classify all Kestrel Hollow inquiries, monitor the android, prepare a decommission order. Okafor hesitates — her own grandmother emigrated from a colony that went quiet. Emotional beat: complicity versus conscience.

chapters.title: The Elder Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Cross-referencing crew manifests, Mira identifies Elder Sef Amara as the only Vesper adult whose records predate the colony's founding by one year — and whose name appears, redacted, in a child's dream recitation. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus attempts a self-diagnostic on her memory block; the Combine's remote kill-switch pings her in warning. She realizes the dreams are leaking from her own sealed archive — a failsafe she herself may have triggered years ago. Emotional beat: horror at being both witness and evidence.

chapters.title: Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Vesper's ancient reactor, long in maintenance mode, spontaneously initiates a shutdown countdown keyed to an encrypted broadcast protocol. The council blames the dreams; the children insist the reactor is 'asking a question.' Emotional beat: a colony holding its breath.

chapters.title: The Debt-Holder's Offer
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Combine offers Cyrus full debt forgiveness in exchange for surrendering her memory core for 'sanitized review' — which would destroy the massacre evidence. She stalls, and Okafor quietly tips her off about a decommission team en route. Emotional beat: the price of loyalty made explicit.

chapters.title: Sef Amara's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Sef Amara's POV. The elder, cornered by Mira, admits she was a Combine records officer who helped bury Kestrel Hollow — a strike on striking freight workers misreported as pirate attack. She kept one unredacted archive hidden inside the reactor's maintenance system. Emotional beat: guilt worn smooth by decades of silence.

chapters.title: Sef Amara's Confession, Part Two
chapters.summary: Sef's POV continues. She reveals why the reactor is counting down: the archive is rigged to a dead-man protocol she set decades ago — if the truth is never spoken, the reactor's failure will make the colony's silence literal. She no longer knows how to stop it. Emotional beat: the corrupting weight of power once held.

chapters.title: The Loop Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Combine blockades Vesper, citing reactor instability, and cuts the colony from the Loop entirely — the same erasure-by-isolation used after Kestrel Hollow. Cyrus must choose: flee on her scheduled freight run or stay. She stays. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over survival.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. Mira organizes the children's dreams into a coherent account: the massacre's victims were the founders' own ancestors, striking Combine freight crews. The children, unburdened by official history, become the colony's only honest archive. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed from below.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Ordered to falsify the incident report, Okafor instead copies the raw reactor telemetry and the children's testimony into her personal ledger. Her grandmother's colony, she realizes, went quiet the same way. Emotional beat: an auditor choosing which numbers to count.

chapters.title: The Decommission Team
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The Combine's retrieval squad boards, hunting Cyrus's memory core. A brutal chase through Vesper's underlevels; Cyrus protects the children sheltering there, taking damage that cracks her shoulder plate — matching the dream image exactly. Emotional beat: becoming the thing the dreams foretold, on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Archive in the Reactor
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Sef's alternating POV. They reach the reactor's maintenance vault and find the unredacted archive — but the countdown accelerates when accessed. Sef confesses she built the failsafe out of despair, not justice. Emotional beat: the architect confronting her own corrupted creation.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus jacks her cracked memory core into the reactor's broadcast array, fusing her sealed combat memory with Sef's archive into one unbroken record. The countdown becomes the carrier wave: the massacre plays on every open band in the Loop. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: What the Records Say Now
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The Combine's cover-up collapses as colonies along the Loop respond — some with grief, some with rage, some with their own buried truths. Okafor files her ledger as evidence and resigns. Emotional beat: a system cracking open.

chapters.title: The Debt Voided
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Under the restored records, Cyrus's indenture — collateral from the Kestrel Hollow 'pirate suppression' — is legally void. She is free to leave the Loop forever. Emotional beat: freedom arriving strangely, like an empty room.

chapters.title: The Slow Orbit
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The colonies begin tentative diplomatic contact, a slow orbit of reconciliation. Sef Amara surrenders to a colony tribunal; the children, dreaming no more, plant a garden over the memorial field. Emotional beat: grief metabolized into inheritance.

chapters.title: Route Still Open
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, final chapter. Offered command of a new diplomatic relay, Cyrus instead signs on to run the freight route between Vesper and the worlds now speaking again — free, chosen, and no longer alone. The last line mirrors the first. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
